abstract.p: The helmet with spherical vizor solves the technical problem of increasing protective effects of the helmet against mechanical, thermal, light, resounding and chemical effects from the direct environment at performing fire and other activities with simultaneous simplification of construction and reduction of production costs. The Figure shows the helmet consisting of the shell (1), ring support (2), spherical vizor (3), six-arm cross with the head basket, latchets for helmet binding, neck protection piece (4) and connective elements. The ring support (2) is with screws (25) and joints with axes (O) round which the spherical vizor (3) is rotating, connected to the lower part of the inner jacket of the shell (1). All connections of arms of the six-arm cross, latchets for binding and the neck protection piece (4) are made on the inner jacket of the ring support (2). By binding these parts to the simple ring support (2), the manufacture is simplified and the manufacture costs reduces and mechanical resistance of the helmet is increased. The spherical form of the vizor (3) with reinforced outside and inner edge enables the use of that helmet in combination with masks for protection of respiratory organs.

L'invention concerne un casque à visière sphérique permettant d'augmenter l'effet protecteur du casque contre les risques mécaniques, thermiques, lumineux, chimiques et de résonance dus à l'environnement direct lors d'activités liées au feu et d'autres activités analogues, le casque présentant une structure simplifiée et pouvant être produit à un coût réduit. Le dessin 3 constitue une illustration du casque selon l'invention qui comprend : une coque (1), un support (2) annulaire, une visière (3) sphérique, une croix à six bras sur la partie couvrant la tête, des crochets de retenue du casque, une pièce (4) de protection de la nuque et des éléments de connexion. Le support (2) annulaire comporte des écrous (25) et des joints à axes (O), autour desquels la visière (3) sphérique tourne, reliés à la partie inférieure de l'enveloppe intérieure de la coque (1). Toutes les connexions des bras de la croix à six bras, des crochets de retenue du casque et de la pièce (4) de protection de la nuque s'effectuent sur l'enveloppe intérieure du support (2) annulaire. En fixant ces parties au support (2) annulaire simple, on simplifie la fabrication et on réduit le coût de fabrication du casque tout en augmentant sa résistance mécanique. La forme sphérique de la visière (3), avec des rebords extérieur et intérieur renforcés, permet d'utiliser ce casque en combinaison avec des masques de protection des organes respiratoires.

description.p: HELMET WITH SPHERICAL VIZOR

Technical Field The invention refers to the helmet that may be used as multipurpose helmet, with which the whole head and neck is protected against undesired mechanical, thermal, light, resounding and chemical effects from the direct surrounding.

According to the sixth edition of the International Patents Classification, the invention belongs to the spheres of technique, marked with the following marks: • A42B-003/00 - helmets; covers for helmets,
• A42B-003/22 - vizors,
• A42B-003/32 - folding helmets; helmets made of separable parts,
• F41 H-001/08 — plastic protection helmets; plastic head guards.

When performing various activities, there are very large possibilities for various injuries of head and neck, as well as eyes, sense of hearing and respiratory organs. Injuries may occur as a consequence of mechanical, thermal, light, resounding and chemical effects. Therefore is the group of anticipating most influencing factors influencing the manufacture of protection helmet, very large.

Protective properties of a helmet depend on design solution of the helmet as the whole and its particular important parts. The efforts of the developer are oriented in the direction of finding simple solutions with reasonable manufacture price and high protective properties. The invention of a helmet with spherical vizor of simple design and with high protective properties solves the technical problem of man's head and neck protection against mechanical, thermal, light, resounding and chemical effects from the direct environment at performing fire and other activities under similar risky conditions.
Background Art

The patent HR P931162 of the same inventor describes the protection helmet with double curved vizor in the form of a part of thin shell of outside jacket of closed torus. The vizor is in sliding connection with space channels between the vizor's guides and inner shell jacket, so that it can be pulled under the shell and pulled out under the same. With the mobile
pulling in - pulling out vizor, the protective effects of the helmet are considerably increased.

In the patent application HR P960371A of the same inventor the multipurpose protection helmet is described, the number of protective effects of which may be adapted, as circumstances require, to the application conditions by adding the equipment consisting of: double curved vizor, earmuffs, antiphones, neck protection pieces and latchets for helmet binding.

In both mentioned solutions the vizor may move between two guides fastened to the inner shell jacket and two sliding surfaces on the inner shell jacket. The front arms of the six-arm cross are connected to vizor guides and the middle and rear arms of the six-arm cross to the inner shell jacket. In the solution described in the patent application HR P960371A the front ends of the latchets for binding the helmet on the head, are connected to the vizor guides and the rear end of this latchets as well as the neck protection piece are connected to the inner shell jacket.

In described solutions, the connection between the vizor and the shell, made as the sliding connection, is achieved by means of two vizor guides. Connections of arms of the six-arm cross, latchets for binding and neck protection piece are made also on vizor guides on the inner shell jacket. Such a complex solution of connecting receiving elements and additional protection on three separate parts, makes more expensive the production of the helmet itself, without important increase of its protective properties.
Disclosure of the Invention

The increase of protective effects of the helmet by the vizor that may be used, according to circumstances, is imposing as the necessity in circumstances in which there is the possibility of injuring face and eyes. The vizor that may be pulled under the shell and pulled out under the shell, represents the best solution because of the protection of the vizor itself and the helmet compactness. In order to pull under the shell a stronger and more solid vizor, it was necessary to find more favourable solution of the connection between the vizor and the shell than the sliding one, as well as a simpler way of fastening the arms of six-arm cross, latchets for binding and neck protection piece, to the shell.
By the invention of helmet with spherical vizor the problem of connection of the vizor and the shell was solved in a practical and simple way, because this connection is made as the rotating connection. The problem of fastening the arms of the six-arm cross, latchets for binding and neck protection piece is solved by means of the ring support that is by joining - disjoining connection in the rear part connected to the lower part of the inner shell jacket. The space between the front part of the ring support and innter shell jacket is free for unhindered moving of reinforced spherical vizor. All connections of arms of the six-arm cross, latchets for binding and neck protection piece are executed on the inner jacket of the ring support. By such execution of of the helmet with ring support, the construction and execution of harder shell and harder spherical vizor is essentially simplified. By carrying over all connections of reception elements and additional protection to the simple ring support, the manufacture was also simplified and the helmet manufacture costs reduced. By introduction of the ring support, the mechanical resistance of the helmet is increased. The spherical vizor form with reinforced outside and inner edge enables the use of this helmet in combination with masks for respiratory organs protection. Fig. 1 shows the helmet with pulled out spherical vizor from the right side.
Fig. 2 shows the helmet with pulled out spherical vizor in front.

Fig. 3 shows the section A-A of the helmet with spherical vizor from the Fig. 2. Fig. 4 shows partly section B-B of the right joint of the helmet with spherical vizor
The helmet with spherical vizor shown on figures 1, 2, 3 and 4 consists of the shell 1, ring support 2, spherical vizor 3, six-arm cross with the basket for head, latchets for binding the helmet, neck protection piece 4 and connection elements. The shell 1 has basically the form of semisphere with uniform wall thickness with reference to the vertical longitudinal plane of the symmetry A-A of the helmet. On the outside surface the shell 1 has the longitudinal central elevated and rounded off frame 5, extending from the front to the rear side of the shell 1. The frame 5 is in the top part the narrowest and to the back and front part it is gradually widening. In the top part, the frame 5 is the highest and on its front side there is the surface 6 for putting marks. On the outside surface of shell 1, along the corrugated edge of the opening, there is the reinforcement 7 in
form of the wide belt, which from the right and left side of the shell 1 follows the edge contour and which in its front and back part unites in arches with the longitudinal central
100 frame 5.

The edge of the opening of the shell 1 in profile shown on Fig. 1 is formed in such a way, that the shell 1 does not cover field of sight, but covers the ears and the back of head. The front part 8 of the edge that is on the front side shortly bended outwards, covers the upper forehead part up to temples and then it is descending on both sides over arc roundnesses up

105 to the auricles. Middle parts 9 of the edge covering the ears are circulary rounded and over mild arc roundnesses connected with a bit elevated back part 10 of the shell 1 edge which is also shortly bended outwards. On the parts of the shell 1 covering the ears there are circular openings 11 , which axis O is vertical to the longitudinal plane of the symmetry of the A-A helmet.

110 The ring support 2 has basically the form of a section of oval shell with uniform thickness of the wall which upper edge 12 is flat and the lower edge 13 follows the edge profile of the shell 1 opening. On the middle parts 14 of the ring support 2 covering the ears, there are hollow cylindrical tangs 15 which axis O is vertical to the longitudinal plane of the symmetry A-A. In the hollows of cylindric tangs 15 there are threads.

115 Along the lower edge 13 of the ring support 2 there are more pressed in, evenly arranged female parts 16 of flexible clamps for fastening the neck protection piece 4 to the inner piece of the ring support 2. The piece 4 is flexible surface in the form of a segment of circular ring with circullary rounded off tops. Along the edge of the internal circular arch of the piece 4 there are more pressed in evenly arranged male parts 17 of flexible clamps
120 joining into female parts 16 of flexible clamps on the ring support 2.

Along the upper edge 12 of the ring support 2, there are connecting spots for fastening the six-arm cross and latchets for binding the helmet to the inner piece of the ring support 2. Rear and middle ends 18 of the six-arm cross are drawn into slots 19, made on the inner piece of the ring support 2 and the front ends 20 of the six-arm cross are fastened with

125 screws 21 to the inner piece of the ring support 2. The rear end 22 and front ends 23 of the three-arm latchet for binding the helmet are fastened with screws 24 to the inner piece of the ring support 2.
130 The ring support 2 is arranged in the lower part of the shell 1, so that with the rear half it lies on the inner jacket of the shell 1. It is connected with the shell 1 by means of two screws 25 and two cylindric tangs 15 that are drawn into the circular openings 11 on the shell 1. In the front part of the helmet between the ring support 2 and the shell 1 there is a free space where there is the spherical vizor 3 embeded on cylindrical tangs 15 of the ring

135 support 2, round which it can rotate. Joint connections with axes O enable rotation of the vizor 3 between two end positions in which the vizor 3 is fully pulled out or fully pulled under the shell 1 of the helmet.
The transparent spherical vizor 3 has basically the form of the segment of thin sphere shell with uniform wall thickness, which is bordered with the upper flat edge 26 and lower

140 corrugated edge 27. Along the upper edge 26 on the external vizor 3 coating there is the reinforcement in form of three-edge frame 28 that on the front side goes over to the stepped limiter 29. In fully pulled out position, the vizor 3 is with the limiter 29 leant against the convexity 30 that is in the inner jacket of the shell 1 in the vicinity of its front part 8 of the edge. By leaning of the limiter 29 against the convexity 30, the vizor 3 is fixed in stable

145 lower position, from which it can be moved only to the upper position in which it is fully pulled under the shell 1. In fully pulled out position, the vizor 3 covers the whole face of a man. The space below the fully pulled out vizor 3 enables the use of modern masks for protection of respiratory organs and eyes against harmful gases. The lower corrugated edge 27 of the vizor 3 goes over to the short guard 31 protruding

150 forward and bended down. The guard 31 is formed in such a way that in fully pulled in position with the surface 32 it touches the front part 8 and the middle part 9 of the opening edge of the shell 1. In such a way formed lower corrugated edge 27 with the guard 31 represents the reinforcement increasing mechanical resistance of the vizor 3, which in end positions does not reduce the field of sight of the user of the helmet. In fully pulled in
155 position, the vizor 3 is fixed in a way, that with the frame 28 it is hooked up to two convexities 33 on the flanks of the inner jacket of the shell 1.

The assembly of rotated joints of the axis O is performed in the way, that the ends of the vizor 3 on which there are circular opening 34 are slipped over the tangs 15 of the ring support 2. The ring support 2 and the vizor 3 thereby flexibly distort in order to enable their

160 bond. Connected ring support 2 and the vizor 3 are properly oriented put into the shell 1 in
the way, that the tangs 15 are put inside in the circular openings 11 on the shell 1 , whereby the flexibility of these parts is also used. By screwing the screws 35 into the threads 15 all connected parts of the left and right joint are tightening till achievemt of satisfactory
165 frictional bond in joints between the vizor 3, shell 1 and ring support 2.

By screwing the srews 35 the whole assembly of the shell 1, ring suppport 2 and the vizor 3 should be additionaly fastened, upon which in the helmet there are inserted and tightened six-arm cross with basket for the head and latchets for binding the helmet on the head. The joining-disjoining bond of the neck protection piece 4 with the ring support 2 enables by
170 means of flexible clamps quick putting and taking off the piece 4 on the helmet.

All parts of the helmet except connecting elements are made from polymere materials by compressive injection technology. Simple forms of shell 1, ring support 2 and vizor 3, as well as the simple assembly procedure reduce the helmet production costs with increased protective properties. By the spherical vizor the protecion properties against mechanical,
175 thermal and light effects are increased, with simultaneous application of the means for protection of respiratory organs against harmful gases.

The described constructional solution of the helmet enables the helmet manufacture for most sophisticated conditions of application, as they are in fire-fighting, civil engineering, mining, forestry and other industry branches. The helmet with spherical vizor may also be
180 applied in other professional and non-professional activities.

claim.claim-text: 1. Helmet with spherical vizor, characterized by, that in the lower part of the shell (1) there is inserted the ring support (2) lieing with the rear half of the jacket on the inner jacket of the shell (1) and which is connected to the shell (1) with two screws (25) and two side joints with the joint axis (O) vertical to the longitudinal plane of the helmet symmetry (A-A) that make two hollow cylindric tangs (15) placed on the outside jacket of middle parts (14) of the ring support (2) in which hollows there are threads pulled through circular openings (34) at the ends of the spherical vizor (3) and through circular openings (11) on the flank sides of the shell (1) and screwed on with the screws (35), round which the vizor (3) can rotate between the extreme pulled out and the extreme pulled in position.

2. Helmet with spherical vizor according to claim 1, characterized by, that the shell (1) has basically the form of the semisphere shell with uniform wall thickness symmetrical to the vertical longitudinal symmetry plane (A-A) on which outside surface there is the longitudinal middle elevated and rounded off frame (5) extending from the front to the back side that is in the top part the narrowest and highest and towards the back and front side it is gradually widening and on which front side there is the surface (6) for putting marks and along the corrugated edge of the shell opening (1) consisting of the front part (8) on the front side shortly bended towards outside and covering the upper part of the forehead to temples and then on both sides over the arc roundnesses it descends to the middle circularry rounded off parts (9) of the edge, covering the ears above which there are circular openings (11) with the joint axis (O) vertical to the longitudinal symmetry plane (A-A), which over mild arc roundnesses unite with a bit elevated back part (10) of the shell (1) edge shortly bended outwards, there is the reinforcement (7) in form of a wide belt that on the left and right side of the shell (1) follows the edge contour and which in the front and back part unites in archs with longitudinal middle frame (5).

3. Helmet with spherical vizor according to the claim 1, characterized by, that the ring support (2) has basically the form of a segment of the oval shell with equal wall thickness, symmetric to the vertical longitudinal symmetry plane (A-A) which upper edge (12) is flat and the lower edge (13) follows the edge profile of the shell (1) opening, that along the
upper edge (12) of the ring support (2) there are connecting spots for fastening the six-arm cross with the head basket and latchets for binding the helmet, made in the way that the rear and middle ends (18) of the six-arm cross with the head basket pulled in the grooves (19) made on the inner jacket of the ring support (2) and the front ends (20) of the six-arm cross with the head basket are fastened with screws (21) to the inner jacket of the ring support (2), the rear end (22) and the front ends (23) of the three-arm latchet for helmet binding are fastened with screws (24) to the inner jacket of the ring support (2) and that along the lower edge (13) of the ring support (2) there are more pressed in equally arranged female parts (16) of flexible clamps for fastening the flexible neck protection piece (4) in formn of the circular ring with circullary rounded off tops, along which inner arch edge there are more pressed in equally arranged male parts (17) of flexible clamps that unite into female parts (16) of flexible clamps on the ring support (2).

4. Helmet with spherical vizor acording to the claim 1, characterized by, that the transparent spherical vizor (3) has basically the form of a segment of thin shell of the sphere with equal wall thickness, symmetrical in relation to the vertical longitudinal plane symmetry (A-A), that is bordered by the upper flat edge (26) and the lower corrugated edge (27), that along the upper flat edge (26) on the outside vizor jacket (3) there is the reinforcement in form of three-edged frame (28) which on the front side goes over to the stepped limiter (29) by which in fully pulled out position the vizor (3) leans against the convexity (30) in the inner shell jacket of the shell (1) in the vicinity of its front part (8) of edge, that the lower corrugated edge (27) of the vizor (3) goes over into the short guard (31) protruding forward and bended downwards and which is formed in the way, that in fully pulled in position with the surface (32) touches the front part (8) and the middle part (9) opening edge of the shell (1) and that in fully pulled in position the vizor (3) is fastened in such a way, that with the frame (28) it is hooked up on two convexities (33) on the sides of the inner jacket of the shell (1). 5. Helmet with spherical vizor according to the claims 1 to 4, characterized by, that all parts of the helmet and screws (35) except connective elements, are made of polymer materials with compressive injection technology.

6. Helmet with spherical vizor according to the claims 1 to 5, characterized by, that it is used in fire-fighting, civil engineering, mining, forestry and other industry branches, as well as in professional and non-professional activities.
7. Helmet with spherical vizor according to the claims 1 to 5, characterized by, that it is used in combination with masks for protection of respiratory organs and eyes against harmful gases.
